Scurvy: determining vitamin C in urine
Bleeding gums, punctate subcutaneous hemorrhages. Ascorbic acid is titrated by the Tillmans method.
Bleeding and swollen gums, loose teeth, weakness, small hemorrhages on the legs, slow healing of minor wounds.
Lives alone. For the last 5–6 months has eaten mainly bread, pasta and tea; has hardly eaten any fruit or vegetables. Smokes.
The gums are bluish-red, loose and bleed on touch. Punctate hemorrhages around the hair follicles on the shins (perifollicular petechiae), “corkscrew” hairs. The skin is dry.
Platelet count is normal. A 24-hour urine sample has been collected (diuresis is given as the 24-hour urine volume).
Determine ascorbic acid in the urine by the **Tillmans method** (titration with 2,6-dichlorophenolindophenol).
Calculate the amount of vitamin C excreted in the 24-hour urine and compare it with the reference range.
Explain the biochemical mechanism of the clinical signs.

**Ascorbic acid (vitamin C)** is a water-soluble vitamin that is not synthesized in the human body (the enzyme L-gulonolactone oxidase is absent). It is a strong **reducing agent**: it is itself easily oxidized to dehydroascorbic acid and reduces other substances.

**Collagen synthesis:** keeps the iron in the active site of prolyl and lysyl hydroxylases in the Fe²⁺ state. Without hydroxyproline and hydroxylysine, the collagen triple helix is not stable and does not form fibers.
Synthesis of **norepinephrine** from dopamine (dopamine β-hydroxylase), synthesis of **carnitine**, intestinal absorption of iron (Fe³⁺ → Fe²⁺).
Antioxidant: scavenges free radicals, regenerates vitamin E.
Ascorbate keeps the iron of prolyl hydroxylase in the reduced (Fe²⁺) state. In deficiency, collagen is not hydroxylated — the vessel wall, gums and skin become fragile.

**2,6-Dichlorophenolindophenol** (Tillmans reagent) is blue in the oxidized state and pink in acid medium; ascorbic acid reduces it to the **colorless leuco form**. Acidified urine is titrated with the dye: as long as ascorbate is present, each added drop is decolorized. When all the ascorbate has been oxidized, the excess dye gives a **pink color** — if it persists for **30 seconds**, the titration is finished.

Ascorbic acid + DCPIP (blue) → Dehydroascorbic acid + DCPIP·H₂ (colorless)

X (mg/day) = A × 0.088 × V / B
A — 0.001 N DCPIP used, mL;  0.088 — ascorbic acid corresponding to 1 mL of 0.001 N dye, mg;
V — daily diuresis, mL;  B — urine taken for titration, mL (10 mL)

Explain the mechanism of the rise of enzyme activity in the blood and its diagnostic significance.

**α-Amylase** (hydrolase class) hydrolyzes the internal **α-1,4-glycosidic bonds** in starch and glycogen: starch → dextrins → maltose. Activator — **Cl⁻ ions**, cofactor — Ca²⁺. Main sources: the salivary glands and the pancreas. Because the molecule is small (≈ 50 kDa), it is filtered in the renal glomeruli and appears in the urine (**diastase**).

**In acute pancreatitis**, trypsinogen is activated prematurely inside the gland; trypsin activates other proenzymes (proelastase, prophospholipase A₂, chymotrypsinogen) — **autolytic digestion** begins. Amylase and lipase pass from the damaged acinar cells into the blood and then into the urine.
Normally, trypsinogen is activated only in the duodenum by enteropeptidase.

The urine is serially diluted two-fold and the same amount of **starch** is added to each tube. After 30 minutes at 38 °C it is tested with **iodine**: starch — **blue**, dextrins — **violet-red**, maltose — no color (the **yellow** color of iodine remains). The tube with the **highest dilution** in which starch is completely digested is found.

Activity (A) = mL of 0.1% starch solution digested by 1 mL of undiluted urine in 30 minutes at 38 °C\nA = 2 mL × D   (D — dilution of the highest-dilution tube with yellow color)\nFor example, if the last yellow tube is 1 : 32: A = 2 × 32 = 64 units

Blood glucose homeostasis and its determination

The blood glucose level is regulated by **insulin** (lowers it) and the counter-regulatory hormones — glucagon, epinephrine, cortisol, growth hormone (raise it). In muscle and adipose tissue, insulin brings **GLUT4** transporters to the membrane; in the liver it enhances glycogen synthesis and glycolysis and suppresses gluconeogenesis.

**In type 2 diabetes mellitus** the main disturbance is **insulin resistance** (often with visceral obesity) and relative insufficiency of β-cell secretion. After a glucose load, tissues take it up slowly — hyperglycemia persists.
In insulin resistance the same amount of insulin activates less GLUT4 — glucose stays in the blood longer.
The **glucose oxidase–peroxidase (GOD-PAP, Trinder)** method — for diagnosis in venous plasma.

**Glucometer** — glucose oxidase (or glucose dehydrogenase) immobilized on the test strip passes electrons to the electrode (electrochemical biosensor). For self-monitoring and screening only; the diagnosis is made in venous plasma.

β-D-glucose + O₂ + H₂O → (glucose oxidase) → gluconolactone + H₂O₂
2H₂O₂ + 4-aminoantipyrine + phenol → (peroxidase) → pink quinoneimine + 4H₂O   (λ = 505 nm)

C (mmol/L) = (A sample / A standard) × 5.55
